Welcome
Welcome to our website and welcome to a celebration of who we are now and a clear vision of what we aspire to be in the future.
Tanbridge House School is an inspiring place. This is true from the viewpoints of both students and adults. We all share the same goals and continue to strive to be ‘exceptional every day’.

Latest Newsletter

Computer Science
The Computer Science department at Tanbridge House School aim to equip students with the skills to participate in a rapidly changing technical world through challenging and engaging topics. We examine how computing impacts their lives and wider society, we teach them to be critical and evaluative about cultural differences and how the digital divide affects communities.
We teach them to become problem solvers, to use logic and reasoning to solve a problem. This is not only a transferrable skill across the whole curriculum it is a skill they will be able to take forward in their day to day life and career beyond Tanbridge.
Computer Science GCSE equips students to have a solid foundation in Computing opening a wide range of job opportunities including, designers, programming, cyber security, engineering, project management and much more.
At KS4 students are given the chance to choose Computer Science alongside their compulsory IT BTEC qualification.

To understand and accurately define technical terminology.

Drama
Drama promotes language development; its collaborative nature provides opportunities for students to develop key skills of communication, negotiation, compromise and self-assertion. Students develop confidence when speaking and their vocabulary is extended when they adopt roles and characters. Students also acquire a critical and subject-specific vocabulary through reflecting on and appraising their own work and others’ work in Drama.
There is global recognition that social wellbeing is founded on personal maturity and emotional literacy. Human concerns and relationships are the foundations of much drama. Drama lessons provide a safe context to explore such issues. Drama involves students working creatively together and problem solving in groups of various sizes. These skills, along with flexibility, empathy and risk-taking, are intrinsic to good drama practice. They are also recognised as vital in the workplace and throughout adult life.

English
English is the bedrock of life and learning, from reading for pleasure and knowledge to interpreting and understanding language and its myriad uses, thereby enabling an ability to communicate confidently and effectively in the world.
Proficiency in both spoken and written English and comprehension when reading is also vital to enable students to access learning in subjects across the curriculum.
The study of English in Literature and Language develops a wide range of important transferable skills such as:
Communication (through Spoken Language study and opportunities, feedback and extended writing opportunities, Debating/Public Speaking Club, Writers’ Club)
To be able to understand and articulate opinions about the importance of Contexts to interpretation of text (e.g The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas (KS3) and The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, An Inspector Calls, Of Mice and Men (KS4)
Creativity (e.g. through fortnightly writing challenges, Creative Writing Club, Journalism Club, task choices both in class and for independent study)
Literacy – in both reading and writing (Word of the Week, Vocabulary logs, spelling logs, literacy lesson starters, purple penning, re-drafting to improve, Stop, Drop and Read, Reading for Pleasure time)
Diversity, resilience, empathy and an appreciation for others’ ideas – within the constraints of a National Curriculum and set content, we still try to allow students to access a range of texts showing aspects of other races, cultures and identities e.g. Twisted Fairy Tales (Yr 7) and Wider Cultures Poetry (Yr 7 and Yr 8), Merchant of Venice (Year 8), Of Mice and Men, Noughts and Crosses and Black Lives Matter topic in Transactional Writing (Year 9), BLM/discrimination-focused poetry for Unseen in Year 10 and 11.

Geography
The intent of our curriculum is to empower students with the skills and knowledge to make sense of the dynamic world around them, and inspire the imagination and desire to want to learn more about the physical, environmental and social interactions of the modern world. As the geographical landscape, both in terms of the natural world and within societies, rapidly changes around us; it is our overarching aim to ensure that pupils are able to gain a broad understanding of the workings of our world, and equip them with lifelong learning skills to understand, evaluate and reach conclusions about geographical themes and processes.
Equalities and Inclusion
We encourage students to ‘think like a geographer’, by this we mean that they learn to consider geographical themes that are fundamentally engrained under the umbrella of ‘Diversity’- demographics, migration, celebration of culture and culture clashes, development, empathy, gender equality and inequality, political and personal freedoms.
The curriculum allows us to give students a truly globalised view of the world that can disrupt attitudes or thinking that do not celebrate and acknowledge the importance of ‘Diversity’ within our society and the wider world

History
Our curriculum intends to arm students with a knowledge of the past. Through this we aim to provide students with transferable skills to take in to their future.
The curriculum aims to strengthen student’s knowledge of how the world around them was formed by teaching them about a variety of key events, people and societies that helped to shape not only the past, but also the modern world. Students will gain an appreciation of different and diverse cultures from around the world which can teach them empathy and acceptance of all.
Literacy and communication are also hugely important parts of our curriculum, and we aim to encourage students to develop these skills through written and verbal work in every lesson.

Absences
Please report absences by 9am via MCAS or you can call the 24 hour absence line (01403 248111).

Illness
Is my child too ill for school?
To report an illness, please either use MCAS or call the 24 hour absence line on the first day of absence, before 9am, stating you child’s name, tutor group, the reason for absence and your relationship to the child.
For consecutive absence, a call is not required every day however, please either report using MCAS or you can email THSattendance@ths.uk.net to confirm if your child is still unwell. Please state the reason for absence when reporting.
A letter following any absence is not required unless specifically requested.
Lateness
If your child is unexpectedly late, please call the absence line as soon as is possible. Any student signing in late without a valid reason will be issued with an after school detention.
Medical Appointments
You can report any absence due to a medical appointment in advance using the absence line (01403 248111) - please state what the appointment is so that appropriate coding can be used. You can also ring the absence line on the morning of the appointment.
Please advise us, where possible, in advance of the appointment. Emails should be sent to THSattendance@ths.uk.net. Please note there may be a delay in releasing your child if we have not received advance notification.
For half day absences, a call to the absence line (01403 248111) is sufficient.
Leaving Early
You can ring the absence line (01403 248111) on the morning advising us that your child needs to leave early, full details must be given so that appropriate coding can be issued.
You can advise us in writing, in advance. Letters must be authorised by your child’s Leader of Year or Pastoral Assistant. Emails should be sent to THSattendance@ths.uk.net.
If the Attendance Officer has not be notified, Student Reception will not allow your child to leave the school site without either being picked up in person or by making a phone call to you to check. This may well result in being late for appointments, hence the importance of letting us know in advance.
